name: Revenge
definition: An injured character pursues personally defined justice, forcing a conflict between symmetry, obsession, moral cost, and the possibility of another response.
negative_signals: punishment carried out without personal transformation
diagnostic_questions: Does retaliation organize the protagonist's choices?
Does the story examine what revenge can and cannot repair?

neighbors.distinction: Revenge is defined by redress for injury, not pursuit alone.
Revenge claims personal authority where legal drama contests institutional judgment.

reader_promises.name: Wound and target
reader_promises.description: Establish a meaningful injury and why the chosen target represents its cause.

reader_promises.name: Moral cost
reader_promises.description: Make each retaliatory step alter identity, relationships, or the meaning of justice.

roles.name: Avenger
roles.description: Converts grief or humiliation into a deliberate campaign.

roles.name: Target
roles.description: Bears actual, partial, inherited, or misunderstood responsibility.

roles.name: Countervoice
roles.description: Offers another account of justice, memory, or possible life.

stakes: Whether an injury defines the future
settings: Social world controlled by the target

movements.name: Injury remembered
movements.description: Define the wound, its contested meaning, and the failure of ordinary redress.

movements.name: Commitment to redress
movements.description: Turn pain into a chosen objective with a boundary the avenger believes will hold.

movements.name: Campaign
movements.description: Advance through consequences that complicate guilt and expand the cost.

movements.name: Reckoning
movements.description: Force a final choice about punishment, mercy, truth, or self-destruction.

complications.name: Divided responsibility
complications.description: The injury resulted from more people or causes than the vow allowed.

complications.name: Innocent link
complications.description: Someone valued by either side would bear the retaliation's cost.

complications.name: Growing resemblance
complications.description: The avenger begins to reproduce the target's method or justification.

twists.name: Wound reinterpreted
twists.description: New truth changes responsibility without declaring the original suffering unreal.

twists.name: Target seeks an ending
twists.description: The target's response makes simple punishment emotionally or strategically inadequate.

conclusions.name: Revenge completed
conclusions.description: Retaliation succeeds and its irreversible personal or social price becomes clear.

conclusions.name: Cycle broken
conclusions.description: The avenger rejects the expected symmetry through an active costly choice.

conclusions.name: Mutual destruction
conclusions.description: Obsession consumes target, avenger, or the world that sustained both.

variation_axes.question: How justified is the target selection?

subversions: Make repair harder and more courageous than retaliation.
Let the target's guilt be real while the chosen punishment remains wrong.
cliches_to_avoid: Violence treated as emotional healing without aftermath
A late innocence reveal that trivializes the original wound
quality_checks: The revenge objective evolves through consequences rather than repetition.
The target has specific agency and responsibility.
The conclusion answers what retaliation changed, not only whether it happened.

sources.title: Seeking Vengeance: Revenge Tragedy, Coherence and Scepticism
sources.contribution: Examines revenge as a morally unstable search for symmetry, order, and justice.

sources.title: Themes and Conventions of Elizabethan Tragedy
sources.contribution: Provides historical grounding for revenge conventions, reversals, and tragic consequence.
